Earlier I had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning: The user wants to log food items. They mention 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea. Also earlier they had two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee. We need to log each item. The function log_food expects food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit, meal_type optional, log_date optional. We need to call the function twice? Actually four items: frozen mango (8 pieces), chai tea (maybe 1 cup?), pepperoni pizza (2 slices), coffee (1 cup). We need to decide portion units. For mango: "piece". For chai tea: "cup". For pepperoni pizza: "slice". For coffee: "cup". Meal types: maybe breakfast for coffee? But we don't know. We can default to snack. But we can specify meal_type if known. The user didn't specify meal times. We can default to snack. Provide log_date? We can use current date/time. But we can leave default null. So we need to call log_food four times. Let's do that.
